author: cl-recap
body:
[opus 5.5] What landed here (vibe-talk side only) and what is still wanted from the deployment-managed voice stack, as cl-relay wrote it in the 2026-10-25 diagnosis, for the owner to take to that stack's owners. None of these was changed by this work.

1. Greeting (#513 voice-greeting-wording). The bridge's INITIAL_GREETING_PROMPT constant ("Say exactly this sentence and nothing else: Hello, let's connect you to your voice assistant.") is sent as a hidden text turn on the first audio_start of EVERY session, reconnects included, so the agent introduces "your voice assistant" as someone else. Wanted: change the sentence to "Say exactly this sentence and nothing else: Hello, you're connected to your chat."; better, read an optional greeting from the profile (the bridge's Profile struct does not deny unknown fields, so a `greeting: Option<String>` with serde default is compatible) and have vibe-talk serve `greeting` in GET /api/v1/voice-agent. vibe-talk's prompt carries a stopgap meanwhile (unverified against the live model).

2. End-of-turn silence. The model session is opened with server VAD and silence_duration_ms unset (the service default). Measured pauses that split one spoken sentence into four turns: 1.45 s, 0.41 s and 0.50 s, so the default end-of-turn silence is at most about 0.4 s, far too short for a driver thinking mid-sentence. Wanted: send silence_duration_ms of about 1000 ms (900 to 1200), or semantic VAD, for this use; 1.0 s would have merged the three short segments.

3. Dropped input transcripts. The speech orchestrator drops user input transcripts for speech that begins after a turn completed and before the next one starts ("dropped output from an invalidated turn"): 18 of 25 completed user transcripts in that host's log (2026-10-22: 11 of 15; 2026-10-25: 7 of 10). The model still hears and answers that speech, so the page's transcript and the model's view diverge, and the page cannot tell the owner is speaking. Wanted: forward input transcripts regardless of turn validity; they are the user's words, not model output.

4. Recap (alternative to what landed). The bridge could list "replay" in session_started.capabilities and handle {"type":"replay","text",...} by appending the text to the session's system prompt (or a hidden conversation item) and answering {"type":"replay_ack","accepted":true}. vibe-talk prefers the frame whenever a bridge lists it.

Landed in vibe-talk for this issue: with replay.enabled and the new replay.bridge_fetches_profile in the server's file, the page arms a one-shot recap (POST /api/v1/voice-recap) just before each call's or reconnect's socket opens, the bridge's next write-scope profile fetch carries it in prompt.text (never the server's own hello's fetch), and the page draws "Caught the agent up" only once the server says a fetch served it. Separately the page now holds relays and notices while the microphone hears the owner (conversation.speech_hold_dbfs, default -42 dBFS) or his partial transcript is still growing, capped by conversation.speech_hold_cap_seconds (default 20), which covers the "hold on" drop even while item 3 stands. The deployment needs replay.enabled = true and replay.bridge_fetches_profile = true for the recap; the threshold needs real in-car numbers (the call-end record now logs speech_holds, speech_hold_max_ms, speech_hold_capped).
